translations.text: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Christ Jesus, in accordance with the faith of God's chosen people and the knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness,
in the hope of eternal life, which the truthful God promised before the eternal ages.
But at his appointed times he revealed his word through preaching, which was entrusted to me according to the command of God our Savior, writing
to Titus, my genuine son in our shared faith: Grace and peace to you from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
For this reason I left you in Crete, so that you would put the remaining things in order and appoint elders in every town, as I instructed you.
Such a person must be free from accusation, the husband of one wife, with believing children who are not accused of reckless living or disobedience.
For an overseer, as God's steward, must be free from accusation, not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not a drunkard, not violent, and not greedy for dishonest gain.
Rather, he must be hospitable, a lover of what is good, sensible, just, holy, and self-controlled.
He must hold firmly to the trustworthy word in accordance with the teaching, so that he can encourage others through sound teaching and rebuke those who contradict it.
For there are many who are disobedient, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision.
They must be silenced, because they ruin entire households by teaching things they should not teach, out of greed for dishonest gain.
A prophet from among them said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy bellies.”
This testimony is true. For this reason, rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith.
They must not pay attention to Jewish myths or to commands from people who turn away from the truth.
Everything is pure to those who are pure, but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. Rather, even their minds and their consciences are defiled.
They profess to know God, but they deny him by their actions. They are detestable and disobedient, unfit for any good work.
But you must speak what is appropriate to sound teaching.
Older men must be sober, dignified, sensible, and sound in faith, love, and endurance.
Older women likewise must behave in a holy manner, not be slanderers or enslaved to much wine, and teach what is good,
so that they may instruct the younger women to love their husbands and their children,
to be sensible, pure, good managers of their homes, and submissive to their husbands, so that God's word will not be slandered.
Likewise, encourage the younger men to be sensible.
Make yourself an example in everything through good deeds, and in your teaching show freedom from envy, purity, and dignity,
with sound speech that is beyond reproach, so that anyone who opposes us will be ashamed, having nothing bad to say about us.
Slaves must submit to their masters, pleasing them in everything and not talking back.
They must not steal anything, but must show complete trustworthiness, so that in everything they may adorn the teaching of God our Savior.
For the grace of God our Savior has appeared to all people,
teaching us to abandon ungodliness and worldly desires and to live sensibly, righteously, and godly lives in this present age,
as we wait for the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ.
He gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify us for himself as a special people, eager to do good works.
Speak these things, encourage, and rebuke with all authority. Do not let anyone look down on you.
Let them remember to submit to rulers and authorities, to obey, and to be ready for every good work.
They must slander no one, avoid quarreling, be gentle, and show complete courtesy toward everyone.
For we ourselves were once foolish and disobedient, going astray, enslaved to various desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful and hating one another.
But when the kindness and love for humanity of God our Savior appeared,
he saved us, not because of righteous deeds we ourselves had done, but according to his mercy, through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
whom he poured out richly upon us through Jesus Christ our Savior,
so that, having been justified by his grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
This saying is trustworthy, and I want you to affirm these things, so that those who believe in God will take care to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and beneficial to people.
But keep away from foolish questions, genealogies, disputes, and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and pointless.
Reject a heretical person after warning him once and then a second time,
knowing that such a person has gone astray and is sinning, condemned by his own actions.
When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your utmost to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.
Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way promptly, so that they lack nothing.
Let the brothers also learn to devote themselves to good works to meet essential needs, so that they will not be unfruitful.
Everyone with me sends you greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all.
